enunciado: What is an appropriate use for private IPv4 addressing?

explicacao_profunda: Private IPv4 (RFC 1918) is not advertised as public Internet space, so internal hosts are not directly reachable from the global Internet without NAT or a similar edge translation—this reduces direct exposure. The correct answer (“on hosts that communicates only with other internal hosts”) captures that protection/conservation role. Option A (“on the public-facing interface of a firewall”) fails because private addresses do not by themselves enable free communication across public boundaries. Option B (“to allow hosts inside to communicate in both directions with hosts outside the organizati…”) is also incorrect: private addressing does not shrink the global Internet routing table for other enterprises, nor make private-to-private Internet paths routable without tunnels/NAT.
